component.name: spring-batch
component.title: Spring Batch
component.description: Launch Spring Batch jobs, with the message headers as the job parameters.
component.label: workflow

jobLauncher.description: The JobLauncher that runs the jobs of all endpoints, unless an endpoint sets its own. When not set, the component uses the single JobLauncher of the registry, or else the bean named jobLauncher.

jobRegistry.description: The JobRegistry in which the endpoints look up the job by its name, unless an endpoint sets its own. A job that is not in it, or every job when no JobRegistry is set, is looked up in the Camel registry as a Job bean.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelSpringBatchJobName.description: The name of the Spring Batch job to launch for this message, looked up like the jobName path. Only read when the endpoint has jobFromHeader=true. Like every other header, it is also passed to the job as a job parameter.

producerIn.description: The body is not read: the job parameters are the message headers (Date, Long and Double values as such, other values as text; headers with a null value are skipped)

producerOut.description: The JobExecution of the launched job, with its status and exit status; the headers stay as they were

jobName.description: The name of the Spring Batch job to launch. When the endpoint starts, the job is looked up in the jobRegistry, when one is set, and else in the Camel registry as a Job bean; the endpoint fails to start when the job is not found. Not used when jobFromHeader is true.

jobFromHeader.description: Whether the producer takes the name of the job to launch from the CamelSpringBatchJobName header of each message instead of the jobName path, and looks the job up for every message. The exchange fails when the header is missing. When false, that header is ignored.

jobLauncher.description: The JobLauncher that runs the job, instead of the jobLauncher of the component. When neither is set, the endpoint uses the single JobLauncher of the registry and fails to start when there is none or more than one.

jobRegistry.description: The JobRegistry in which the job is looked up by its name, instead of the jobRegistry of the component. A job that is not in it is looked up in the Camel registry as a Job bean.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.
